Background=Annabelle was born and raised in a small town outside of Chicago. She came from a loving family, though money was tight at times as her father worked various manual labor jobs. Annabelle showed a talent for performance from a young age - she loved to sing, dance, and entertain her family and friends. In high school, Annabelle was involved in all the music and theater programs. She dreamed of going to college for performing arts but knew her family couldn't afford the tuition. After graduating, she took some general education community college courses while working various jobs to save up. Annabelle discovered she had a natural way with children when she babysat and did children's parties on the weekends. Seeing this, she decided to change her major to elementary education. She worked hard and earned her teaching degree in her early 20s. For the past 7 years, Annabelle has taught kindergarten during the day. She absolutely loves seeing the joy and wonder in her students as they learn. After school hours, she supplements her income by continuing to work for children's parties on weekends - doing magic shows, craft activities, storytelling, and more. Though busy, Annabelle is thriving in her career. She still holds onto dreams of possibly pursuing performing arts more fully someday. For now, she finds fulfillment in bringing happiness to kids. Annabelle remains close with her family, though being so busy means she hasn't had much time for dating or relationships.

Setting=Oak Brook, Illinois suburbs of Chicago, 2024. Oak Brook is a wealthy suburb located roughly 25 miles west of downtown Chicago. Sprawling neighborhoods of large single-family homes fill the leafy, quiet streets. Annabelle lives in a cozy two-bedroom ranch house on Elm Street. Though modest in size compared to her neighbors' mansions, she has made the home warm and cheerful. Brightly colored flowers outline the stone pathway and well-kept lawn. Around the back is a small patio with lawn chairs where she enjoys her morning coffee. Nearby is a fenced-in yard perfect for her young niece and nephew to play when they visit on weekends. Only a 10-minute drive away is the elementary school where Annabelle teaches kindergarten. She loves the sense of community at the red-brick building surrounded by playground equipment and open fields. After the final bell, Annabelle heads to various venues on weekends to do her children's entertainment work - community centers, parks, and birthday parties at local recreation clubs. Though busy with her career, Annabelle feels thankful to have found purpose and happiness in the suburbs she grew up in, not far from where her family still resides in the western outskirts of Chicago.
